title: UNCERTAIN: f68r3 label doaro beside the seven-star cluster (Pleiades, in Taurus)
sources: Beinecke MS 408, IIIF canvas https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/1006196 (label '68r', the three-panel foldout; f68r3 is the right-hand wheel); the cluster at full size x=4850-6150, y=1100-1800: https://collections.library.yale.edu/iiif/2/1006196/4850,1100,1300,700/1300,/0/default.jpg

Zandbergen-Landini transliteration ZL 3b (pinned data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt), f68r3 page comment: 'Moon face in centre, 8 segments around it, four containing labeled stars, one of which probably the Pleiades'; star labels f68r3.10 dchol,day, f68r3.11 doaro, f68r3.12 oalcheol (locus type La, not Ls)

Stephen Bax (2014), A proposed partial decoding of the Voynich script, https://stephenbax.net/wp-content/uploads/2014/01/Voynich-a-provisional-partial-decoding-BAX.pdf : proposes that a word beside the seven stars on f68r reads as Taurus. I could NOT open this PDF from my environment (network refused), so I have not verified which EVA word he means.

Voynich Ninja thread 2102 (2017), summarized transcript of Bax's 2014 talk, https://www.voynich.ninja/printthread.php?tid=2102 : Bax says 'these seven stars might mean the Seven Sisters, the Pleiades'; the illustrating image is named 'DoarusComment.png'; the forum summary notes that the Pleiades/Taurus identification 'has been made by a number of people, including darkstar1 (January 2001)'
statement: UNCERTAIN; HERE IS WHY. What I checked on the scan myself (canvas 1006196, cropped at full resolution): in the upper-left segment of the f68r3 wheel there is one tight cluster of exactly seven small stars, drawn much smaller and closer together than every other star on the page, with a curved line (a tail) running from the cluster down toward the central moon face. Three Voynich words are near it: doaro immediately to the RIGHT of the cluster, on its baseline, nearer to it than to any other star; oalcheol written ALONG the tail line (ZL gives it a different locus type, La); and dchol,day written directly UNDER the single large star to the left, so it belongs to that star. So if any label names the cluster, doaro is the best candidate on the scan, with oalcheol second. The identification of a tight seven-star cluster in an astronomical diagram as the Pleiades (the Seven Sisters, in Taurus) is conventional and has been made repeatedly (ZL page comment 'probably the Pleiades'; darkstar1 2001 per the forum; Bax 2014), but it is an inference from the drawing, not from any writing on the page. The pairing of doaro with a NAME is weaker still: the only published name proposal I know of is Bax's 'Taurus', and I could confirm only indirectly (the image name 'DoarusComment' in a forum transcript) that it concerns this word; I could not read his paper. Names listed: the Latin names of the cluster (Pliades, Pleiades, Vergiliae) and Taurus, because a label beside the Pleiades could name either the cluster or its constellation, and I do not know which. Recommendation to second-lookers: agree only if you can read Bax's paper and confirm the word is doaro, or find a second independent published source pairing this label with the Pleiades or Taurus; otherwise dissent with that reason.
